title: A query span renders without the `debug.trace` grant, and with the grant an unsampled request renders none.
text: `nvs_stdlib`'s `QueryWatch::named` (`crates/nvs-stdlib/src/db/span.rs:51`) renders a statement's span whenever `nvs_runtime::Ctx::records_spans` answers `true`: the request is sampled, or `DebugFlags::TRACE` is on. The `debug.trace` grant (`nvs_config::capability::Cap::DebugTrace`, `rule:testing/debug-mode-directive`) is read by neither. **The user decided:** the grant gates only the `DebugFlags::TRACE` path. A span rendered because `TRACE` is on needs `nvs_runtime::capability::granted(ctx, Cap::DebugTrace, Scope::Unscoped)`, which costs one configuration read per statement on a traced run only. A sampled request's span needs no grant, and `rule:observability/a-query-is-a-trace-event` states that sampling is the request to export and that the exporter's own settings decide where a span goes. Gating the sampled path too was declined: it would remove every query span from an exported trace on a deployment that grants no debug root, and tie OTLP export to a path-scoped grant that names no destination. Closing the record with only a rule change was declined because `rule:testing/debug-mode-directive` makes writing a trace its own capability. `TRACE` is armed only under `nvs run` and `nvs test` (`data/gaps/nvs-config/debug-mode-is-read-by-nothing.json`), so the gated path waits on that record.
